chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who said to another, 'Sell to me the fruit of your palm tree, this one in which there is, for two qafizs of dates, or less, or more,' naming whatever he wished, so he sold it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Dates and half-ripened dates from one palm tree, there is no problem with it.'
But if one mixes the old dates or the half-ripened dates, it is not valid; and raisins and grapes are similar to that.

key_terms.قَفِيزَانِ: Two qafizs (a traditional unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for validly selling fruit from a palm tree in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of *mukhabarah* (selling fruit on the tree) by permitting sales based on estimation with flexible quantity terms, while distinguishing between permissible mixing of ripeness stages from a single source and impermissible mixing of distinct types like old and new dates. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on preventing *gharar* (uncertainty) in agricultural transactions by ensuring the commodity's nature remains consistent. The hadith serves as a foundational text for commercial law in *Usul al-Kafi*, illustrating the practical application of prophetic traditions in daily trade.
